title: "In a renv project, your ~/.Rprofile is no longer read"
ref: RNV-09
categories: [renv and installation]

attendu: "the personal options from `~/.Rprofile`, on top of {renv}"

source: "Slack ThinkR (2020)"
---

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
# ~/.Rprofile
options(width = 120, digits = 4)

# the project's .Rprofile, created by renv::init()
source("renv/activate.R")
```
:::

This pitfall depends on R's startup files on the machine, so it cannot be replayed in the browser.

## Why

{renv} is not the one choosing: at startup, R reads a single `.Rprofile`, the one in the working directory if it exists, otherwise the one in the home directory. `renv::init()` creates a `.Rprofile` in the project, which therefore takes the place of yours. Your options, shortcuts and personal repositories disappear without a message.

By default {renv} does not load the user profile either, to keep personal code from breaking the project's isolation.

## The remedy

Have {renv} load the user profile, or put environment variables in `~/.Renviron`, which is still read.

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```bash
# ~/.Renviron
RENV_CONFIG_USER_PROFILE=TRUE
```
:::
